claim: Tumor xenografts with a similar genetic background can be distinguished by their differing rates of the metabolism of 13C labeled glucose tracers.
source: Using pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma as a model, we demonstrate that tumor xenografts with a similar genetic background can be distinguished by their differing rates of the metabolism of 13C labeled glucose tracers, which can be imaged without hyperpolarization by using newly developed techniques for noise suppression.
evidence: The abstract states this as a demonstrated finding from the study.

claim: 13C labeled glucose tracers can be imaged without hyperpolarization by using newly developed techniques for noise suppression.
source: Using pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma as a model, we demonstrate that tumor xenografts with a similar genetic background can be distinguished by their differing rates of the metabolism of 13C labeled glucose tracers, which can be imaged without hyperpolarization by using newly developed techniques for noise suppression.
evidence: The abstract describes the technical approach used in the study.

claim: Cancer subtypes that appeared to have similar metabolic profiles based on steady state metabolic measurement can be distinguished from each other using 13C-glucose imaging.
source: Using this method, cancer subtypes that appeared to have similar metabolic profiles based on steady state metabolic measurement can be distinguished from each other.
evidence: The abstract presents this as a finding from the study comparing different measurement methods.

claim: The metabolic maps from 13C-glucose imaging localized lactate production and overall glucose metabolism to different regions of some tumors.
source: The metabolic maps from 13C-glucose imaging localized lactate production and overall glucose metabolism to different regions of some tumors.
evidence: The abstract describes spatial heterogeneity detected by the imaging method.

claim: Tumor heterogeneity in lactate production and glucose metabolism would not be detectable in FDG-PET.
source: Such tumor heterogeneity would not be not detectable in FDG-PET.
evidence: The abstract makes a comparative claim about the limitations of FDG-PET based on the nature of the technique.

claim: Altered metabolism to sustain rapid growth is one of the hallmarks of cancer.
source: Altered metabolism to sustain rapid growth is one of the hallmarks of cancer (Vander Heiden and DeBerardinis, 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to established literature.

claim: Certain common features of tumor metabolism are retained even in different cancers.
source: While certain common features of tumor metabolism are retained even in different cancers (Ward and Thompson, 2012; Pavlova and Thompson, 2016), other features can vary considerably among patients and even within a single tumor (Hensley et al., 2016; Cros et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published research.

claim: Metabolic features can vary considerably among patients and even within a single tumor.
source: While certain common features of tumor metabolism are retained even in different cancers (Ward and Thompson, 2012; Pavlova and Thompson, 2016), other features can vary considerably among patients and even within a single tumor (Hensley et al., 2016; Cros et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published research.

claim: Metabolite levels control a host of cellular processes from cell signaling to growth and differentiation.
source: Since metabolite levels control a host of cellular processes from cell signaling to growth and differentiation (Vander Heiden and DeBerardinis, 2017; Ward and Thompson, 2012), local variations in metabolism can impact the sensitivity of the tumor to different forms of treatment.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published research.

claim: Local variations in metabolism can impact the sensitivity of the tumor to different forms of treatment.
source: Since metabolite levels control a host of cellular processes from cell signaling to growth and differentiation (Vander Heiden and DeBerardinis, 2017; Ward and Thompson, 2012), local variations in metabolism can impact the sensitivity of the tumor to different forms of treatment.
evidence: This is presented as a logical consequence of metabolite control over cellular processes, supported by citations.

claim: Local concentrations of glucose have been shown to influence the efficacy of specific types of chemotherapy and radiotherapy.
source: Local concentrations of glucose (Liu et al., 2017a; Mathews et al., 2014), fatty acids (Svensson et al., 2016), and amino acids (Mathews et al., 2014), for example, have been shown to influence the efficacy of specific types of chemotherapy and radiotherapy, which could lead to a possible change of treatment strategy (Daemen et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published research.

claim: Local concentrations of fatty acids have been shown to influence the efficacy of specific types of chemotherapy and radiotherapy.

evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published research.

claim: Local concentrations of amino acids have been shown to influence the efficacy of specific types of chemotherapy and radiotherapy.

claim: FDG-PET is the only molecular imaging technique in widespread clinical use.
source: The only molecular imaging technique in widespread clinical use, FDG-PET, is largely limited to measurements of glucose uptake only and cannot characterize downstream biochemical transformations (Giordano et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement about the clinical status of FDG-PET is supported by a citation.

claim: Measurements of downstream products like lactate become important in preventing false positives in organs like the brain which have a high natural glucose uptake.
source: This limitation is particularly important for organs like the brain which have a high natural glucose uptake. In these situations, measurements of downstream products like lactate become important in preventing false positives (De Feyter et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to published research.

claim: MALDI-MS has been successful at characterizing tumor metabolic heterogeneity in biopsies.
source: Other techniques with high specificity, such as MALDI-MS, have been successful at characterizing tumor metabolic heterogeneity in biopsies (Giordano et al., 2016; Mirnezami et al., 2014) but cannot be employed in vivo.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published research.

claim: MALDI-MS cannot be employed in vivo.
source: Other techniques with high specificity, such as MALDI-MS, have been successful at characterizing tumor metabolic heterogeneity in biopsies (Giordano et al., 2016; Mirnezami et al., 2014) but cannot be employed in vivo.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of the MALDI-MS technique based on its nature.

claim: Tumor metabolism in vivo can be imaged by 1H magnetic resonance spectroscopy.
source: Tumor metabolism in vivo can be imaged by 1H magnetic resonance spectroscopy, but as a steady state method it contains contributions from multiple processes and cannot distinguish the internal metabolism of the tumor from contributions from the surrounding stroma.
evidence: This statement describes the capabilities and limitations of 1H MRS based on the nature of the technique.

claim: 1H magnetic resonance spectroscopy as a steady state method contains contributions from multiple processes and cannot distinguish the internal metabolism of the tumor from contributions from the surrounding stroma.

evidence: This describes a limitation of 1H MRS based on the nature of steady-state measurements.

claim: The signal from a 13C labeled tracer has been considered too weak for in vivo imaging.
source: In principle, this can be accomplished by MRI through the use of 13C labeled tracers. In practice, the signal from a 13C labeled tracer has been considered too weak for in vivo imaging.
evidence: This describes a historical limitation in the field based on established knowledge.

claim: Hyperpolarized MRI increases the signal by three orders of magnitude or more.
source: Hyperpolarized MRI was developed to surmount this obstacle, taking advantage of the fact that the high spin polarization of a paramagnetic radical can be transferred to the 13C nucleus on another molecule under resonant microwave irradiation, increasing the signal by three orders of magnitude or more.
evidence: This describes the signal enhancement achieved by hyperpolarization based on established knowledge of the technique.

claim: The transfer of spin polarization to 13C happens efficiently only at temperatures near ~1 K.
source: However, this transfer happens efficiently only at temperatures near ~1 K and the hyperpolarization is rapidly lost when the sample is brought to room temperature before injecting.
evidence: This describes a technical requirement of hyperpolarization based on established knowledge.

claim: Hyperpolarization is rapidly lost when the sample is brought to room temperature before injecting.
source: However, this transfer happens efficiently only at temperatures near ~1 K and the hyperpolarization is rapidly lost when the sample is brought to room temperature before injecting.
evidence: This describes a limitation of hyperpolarization based on established knowledge.

claim: Hyperpolarized studies are normally applied to probes whose 13C T1 relaxation time is long enough that the enhanced polarization is not lost before the metabolic flux can be determined.
source: Due to this limitation, these studies are normally applied to probes whose 13C T1 relaxation time is long enough that the enhanced polarization is not lost before the metabolic flux can be determined.
evidence: This describes a practical constraint on hyperpolarized MRI studies based on the technique's limitations.

claim: Pyruvate has proven to be one of the most useful probes for hyperpolarized MRI.
source: Of these probes, pyruvate has proven to be one of the most useful probes as it interrogates the central switching point from glycolysis to the TCA cycle (Gray et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to published research.

claim: Pyruvate interrogates the central switching point from glycolysis to the TCA cycle.

claim: It has been possible to assess the glycolytic profile of tumors in vivo by comparing the pyruvate-to-lactate conversion between tumors or between pre- and post-treatment.
source: By comparing the pyruvate-to-lactate conversion between tumors or between pre- and post-treatment, it has been possible to assess the glycolytic profile of tumors in vivo and assess metabolic flux changes during treatment (Gutte et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to published research.

claim: Hyperpolarized MRI using pyruvate is unable to detect changes occurring upstream of the TCA cycle.
source: However, hyperpolarized MRI using pyruvate is unable to detect changes occurring upstream of the TCA cycle, which are common in many cancers.
evidence: This describes a limitation of pyruvate-based hyperpolarized MRI based on the metabolic position of pyruvate.

claim: Changes occurring upstream of the TCA cycle are common in many cancers.
source: However, hyperpolarized MRI using pyruvate is unable to detect changes occurring upstream of the TCA cycle, which are common in many cancers.
evidence: This statement about cancer metabolism is presented as established knowledge.

claim: Glucose is difficult to hyperpolarize.
source: Although glucose itself is difficult to hyperpolarize, new techniques allow the dynamic imaging of metabolic tracers by MRI without hyperpolarization.
evidence: This describes a technical challenge with glucose hyperpolarization based on established knowledge.

claim: New techniques allow the dynamic imaging of metabolic tracers by MRI without hyperpolarization.
source: Although glucose itself is difficult to hyperpolarize, new techniques allow the dynamic imaging of metabolic tracers by MRI without hyperpolarization.
evidence: This describes the technical approach developed and used in the study.

claim: Non-hyperpolarized imaging suffers from low signal sensitivity but this can be compensated for by efficient noise suppression.
source: This imaging clearly suffers from low signal sensitivity but this can be compensated for by efficient noise suppression (Brender et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to published research.

claim: MIA Paca-2 and Hs 766T are cell lines established from pancreatic ductal adenocarcinomas with similar mutations in major metabolic genes.
source: MIA Paca-2 and Hs 766T are cell lines established from pancreatic ductal adenocarcinomas (PDACs) with similar mutations in major metabolic genes (Deer et al., 2010).
evidence: This statement about the cell lines is supported by a citation.

claim: Hs 766T was derived from a metastatic site.
source: Hs 766T was derived from a metastatic site and is expected to have a different stromal boundary compared to MIA Paca-2, which is derived from a primary heterogeneous tumor.
evidence: This describes the origin of the Hs 766T cell line, which is established knowledge about this cell line.

claim: MIA Paca-2 was derived from a primary heterogeneous tumor.

evidence: This describes the origin of the MIA Paca-2 cell line, which is established knowledge about this cell line.

claim: Hs 766T is expected to have a different stromal boundary compared to MIA Paca-2.

claim: It is possible to detect a difference in glucose metabolism between MIA Paca-2 and Hs 766T using a newly developed technique to image glycolysis using non-hyperpolarized 13C glucose as a tracer.
source: While MIA Paca-2 and Hs 766T have similar overall metabolism (Daemen et al., 2015), it is possible to detect a difference in glucose metabolism using a newly developed technique to image glycolysis using non-hyperpolarized 13C glucose as a tracer (Brender et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation and describes a finding from the study.

source: The MIA Paca-2 tumors appear entirely homogenous and undifferentiated, an observation that holds down to the cellular level ( Figure 1.D).

evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to published research.

claim: Immature, rather than deficient, vasculature may be responsible for the higher hypoxia levels in Hs 766T.

claim: Pancreatic host tissue from the mouse was metabolically distinct from Hs 766T and MiaPaca2 xenografts (p<0.001 based on two-way ANOVA).
source: As expected, pancreatic host tissue from the mouse was metabolically distinct from Hs 766T and MiaPaca2 xenografts (p<0.001 based on two-way ANOVA), with numerous metabolic differences across multiple metabolic pathways (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This statement is supported by statistical analysis of data from the study.

claim: The largest metabolic changes between tumor xenografts and normal tissue are concentrated in pathways connected to amino acid biosynthesis and degradation.
source: The largest changes are concentrated in pathways connected to amino acid biosynthesis and degradation, reflecting an imbalance between amino acid metabolism and protein biosynthesis caused by unsustainable growth.
evidence: This is an observation from the CE-MS data analysis in the study.

claim: Amino acid levels of all types and amino acid synthetic intermediates were strongly attenuated in both Hs 766T and MIA Paca-2 cell lines.
source: Amino acid levels of all types and amino acid synthetic intermediates were strongly attenuated in both cell lines.
evidence: This is an observation from the CE-MS data analysis in the study.

claim: Both Hs 766T and MIA Paca-2 cell lines show a strong depletion in the level of intermediates throughout the urea cycle.
source: Both cell lines also show a strong depletion in the level of intermediates throughout the urea cycle, the primary pathway for protein catabolism, as well as the polyamine biosynthetic pathway downstream of the urea cycle.

claim: The urea cycle is the primary pathway for protein catabolism.

claim: Steady state concentrations of glycolytic intermediates were elevated in both Hs 766T and MIA Paca-2 cell lines.
source: Consistent with previous reports on PDAC tumors (Ying et al., 2012), steady state concentrations of glycolytic intermediates were elevated in both cell lines, so were the metabolites of the pentose phosphate pathway for nucleotide and NADPH production (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).

claim: Metabolites of the pentose phosphate pathway for nucleotide and NADPH production were elevated in both Hs 766T and MIA Paca-2 cell lines.

claim: There were increased levels of metabolites in the methionine redox cycle of the tumor xenografts.
source: To counter the increased oxidative stress, there were increased levels of metabolites in the methionine redox cycle of the tumor xenografts: the reduced equivalents are depressed and the oxidized equivalents elevated compared to normal tissue.
evidence: This is an observation from the CE-MS data analysis in the study.

claim: The reduced equivalents in the methionine redox cycle are depressed and the oxidized equivalents elevated in tumor xenografts compared to normal tissue.
source: To counter the increased oxidative stress, there were increased levels of metabolites in the methionine redox cycle of the tumor xenografts: the reduced equivalents are depressed and the oxidized equivalents elevated compared to normal tissue.

claim: Lactate levels are highly elevated in both Hs 766T and MIA Paca-2 tumors.

claim: No single pathway stood out as being distinct between Hs 766T and MIA Paca-2 tumors.

claim: Only a few biomarkers are distinct at the 5% confidence level between Hs 766T and MIA Paca-2, with most of the differences in the TCA cycle.

claim: The most striking difference between Hs 766T and MIA Paca-2 was in fumarate levels (p=0.003).
source: The most striking difference was in fumarate levels (p=0.003), which were significantly depressed (decreased fourfold relative to normal) in MIA Paca-2 and normal or slightly elevated in Hs 766T (elevated 1.4-fold).
evidence: This statement is supported by statistical analysis of data from the study.

claim: Fumarate levels were significantly depressed (decreased fourfold relative to normal) in MIA Paca-2.
source: The most striking difference was in fumarate levels (p=0.003), which were significantly depressed (decreased fourfold relative to normal) in MIA Paca-2 and normal or slightly elevated in Hs 766T (elevated 1.4-fold).
evidence: This is an observation from the CE-MS data analysis in the study.

claim: Fumarate levels were normal or slightly elevated in Hs 766T (elevated 1.4-fold).
source: The most striking difference was in fumarate levels (p=0.003), which were significantly depressed (decreased fourfold relative to normal) in MIA Paca-2 and normal or slightly elevated in Hs 766T (elevated 1.4-fold).
evidence: This is an observation from the CE-MS data analysis in the study.

claim: Fumarate has been suggested as an oncometabolite.
source: Fumarate has been suggested as an oncometabolite (Yang et al., 2012; Sullivan et al., 2013) created both through the TCA cycle and as a byproduct of the urea cycle that competitively inhibits 2-OG-dependent oxygenases to stabilize the HIF complex and induce pseudohypoxia.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published research.

claim: Fumarate is created both through the TCA cycle and as a byproduct of the urea cycle.
source: Fumarate has been suggested as an oncometabolite (Yang et al., 2012; Sullivan et al., 2013) created both through the TCA cycle and as a byproduct of the urea cycle that competitively inhibits 2-OG-dependent oxygenases to stabilize the HIF complex and induce pseudohypoxia.
evidence: This statement about fumarate metabolism is supported by citations.

claim: Fumarate competitively inhibits 2-OG-dependent oxygenases to stabilize the HIF complex and induce pseudohypoxia.

claim: Malate and arginosuccinate were significantly depressed in MIA Paca-2.
source: Malate and arginosuccinate, two other intermediates linked to fumarate metabolism were also significantly depressed in MIA Paca-2.

claim: Pyruvate metabolism appears to be statistically indistinguishable in the MIA Paca-2 and Hs 766 T cell lines when using C-1 labeled pyruvate as a metabolic tracer.
source: Few differences could be seen when using C-1 labeled pyruvate as a metabolic tracer; pyruvate metabolism appears to be statistically indistinguishable in the MIA Paca-2 and Hs 766 T cell lines.

claim: The rate of pyruvate to lactate conversion was similar in MIA Paca-2 and Hs 766T.

claim: The rate of transamination of pyruvate to alanine was similar in MIA Paca-2 and Hs 766T.
source: The rate of pyruvate to lactate conversion was similar in MIA Paca-2 and Hs 766T as was both the rate of transamination of pyruvate to alanine and the first step of the TCA cycle as measured by bicarbonate production (see Figure 2).
evidence: This statement is supported by data from the hyperpolarized pyruvate experiments shown in Figure 2.

claim: The first step of the TCA cycle as measured by bicarbonate production was similar in MIA Paca-2 and Hs 766T.

claim: Pyruvate metabolism is not a sensitive biomarker for distinguishing subtle differences among hypoxic pancreatic adenocarcinoma subtypes.

claim: Strong signals at 22.8 and 18.9 ppm in the indirect dimension of the HSQC spectrum confirmed that the peaks at 22.8 ppm and 18.9 ppm arise from 13C labeled lactate and alanine, respectively.
source: Strong signals at 22.8 and 18.9 ppm in the indirect dimension of the HSQC spectrum (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A) and carbon satellites in the TOCSY spectrum (Lane and Fan, 2007) (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B) confirmed that the peaks at 22.8 ppm and 18.9 ppm arise from 13C labeled lactate and alanine, respectively (Figure 3A).
evidence: This statement is supported by NMR spectroscopy data from the study.

claim: 13C labeled glutamate and aspartate are detectable in the ex vivo HSQC but not in the in vivo MRS.
source: 13C labeled glutamate and aspartate are detectable in the ex vivo HSQC but not in the in vivo MRS, likely because the longer relaxation times (Badar-Goffer et al., 1990; Allouche-Arnon et al., 2013) strongly attenuate the signal with the short recycle delay used in the in vivo experiment.
evidence: This is an observation from the study with an explanation supported by citations.

claim: The peaks at 95 and 98 ppm arise exclusively from glucose without contribution from glucose-6-phosphate or any other glycolytic intermediates.
source: The absence of any detectable peaks near 75 ppm confirms they arise exclusively from glucose without contribution from glucose-6-phosphate or any other glycolytic intermediates (Timm et al., 2015; Wishart et al., 2018; Wishart et al., 2007).
evidence: This statement is supported by spectral analysis and citations.

claim: The peak at 63 ppm and the spectrally crowded region between 63 and 78 ppm contains contributions from glycerol containing species.
source: While the peaks at 95 and 98 ppm can be definitively assigned to carbon 1 of glucose, the HSQC and the pre-injection spectra (Figure 3A) confirms the other intense peak at 63 ppm and the spectrally crowded region between 63 and 78 ppm contains contributions from glycerol containing species.
evidence: This statement is supported by spectral analysis from the study.

claim: The glycerol resonances were not derived directly from the glucose bolus.
source: The lack of 13C-13C couplings for the glycerol resonances in the HSQC show that these molecules were not derived directly from the glucose bolus.
evidence: This is an inference from the NMR spectroscopy data in the study.

claim: An increase in the intensity of the 98 ppm resonance reflects the arrival of glucose from the bloodstream into the instrument's field of view.
source: Specifically, an increase in the intensity of the 98 ppm resonance reflects the arrival of glucose from the bloodstream into the instrument's field of view (gluconeogenesis within the tumor is assumed to be negligible on this time scale).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the NMR signal based on the experimental design.

claim: Gluconeogenesis within the tumor is assumed to be negligible on the experimental time scale.
source: Specifically, an increase in the intensity of the 98 ppm resonance reflects the arrival of glucose from the bloodstream into the instrument's field of view (gluconeogenesis within the tumor is assumed to be negligible on this time scale).
evidence: This is stated as an assumption for the interpretation of the glucose signal.

claim: A decrease in the 98 ppm resonance intensity reflects either the removal of glucose by the bloodstream out of the field of view or the conversion of glucose into other species.
